answer: In the juniper marketplace, each new identity locks a 20-credit bond for ten rounds before bidding. Random auditors follow the signed evidence thread from a job's inputs to its output; provable fraud burns the bond. If a fake account can steal at most one credit before audit and detection exceeds 5%, expected loss beats that gain. A ridge of aliases must fund separate, simultaneously locked bonds. This prices attacks rather than proving unique operators; colluding auditors remain a weakness.
